name: Kakinada Kaja
instructions: 1. Prepare a dough with maida, a little ghee, and water; let it rest. 2. Prepare a 'saatam' (paste) by mixing ghee and rice flour. 3. Roll the dough into thin sheets, apply the saatam, fold into layers, and roll into a tight cylinder. 4. Cut the cylinder into small cylindrical pieces. 5. Deep fry these pieces in medium-hot oil until golden brown. 6. Prepare a sugar syrup of one-string consistency flavored with cardamom. 7. Soak the fried kaja pieces in the syrup until they absorb it, then let them cool.
description: Kakinada Kaja is an iconic sweet from the coastal city of Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh. Known for its distinct dry outer layer and syrupy, flaky interior, it holds a GI tag and is a beloved traditional sweet served during festivals, weddings, and special occasions across the state.
